# The rational Lie algebra generated by simple root operators (`RootLieAlgebra`)

Author: Worker 239.

This module works with rational square matrices indexed by a finite type `ι`, whose basis
vectors carry weights `wt : ι → X` (see `WeightGrading`). It shows that the span of the iterated
commutators of "simple root operators" is closed under the commutator. It then identifies some
of the weight components of this span. No Mathlib `LieSubalgebra` API is used. Commutators are
handled through the bilinear map `matAd`.

## The commutator and diagonal characters

- `matAd : Matrix ι ι ℚ →ₗ[ℚ] Matrix ι ι ℚ →ₗ[ℚ] Matrix ι ι ℚ`, with
  `matAd_apply : matAd a y = a * y − y * a`. The lemmas `matAd_matAd` (Jacobi identity),
  `matAd_self` and `matAd_swap` (antisymmetry) hold. The lemmas `matAd_mem_of_mem_span` and
  `matAd_mem_of_mem_span_left` say that it suffices to check membership of commutators on
  generating sets.
- `charDiag wt χ` is the diagonal matrix `diag(χ (wt c))` of an additive character
  `χ : X →+ ℚ`. It has weight `0` (`isWtHom_charDiag`). It acts on a matrix of weight `μ` by
  the scalar `χ μ` (`matAd_charDiag`). Two such matrices commute (`matAd_charDiag_charDiag`).

## Iterated commutators

`IterComm g α μ A` is the inductive predicate saying that `A` is an iterated commutator
`[g i₁, [g i₂, …, g i_m] …]` of a family `g : κ → Matrix ι ι ℚ` with total weight
`μ = α i₁ + ⋯ + α i_m`.

- `IterComm.isWtHom`: if each `g i` has weight `α i`, then `A` has weight `μ`.
- `IterComm.exists_coeff`: `μ = Σ c_i α_i` with `c : κ → ℕ` nonzero.
- `IterComm.eq_of_eq_smul`: suppose the `α i` have unique integral coefficients, and
  `μ = k • α i`. Then either `A = g i` and `k = 1`, or `A = 0`. An iterated commutator of
  length at least two with weight a multiple of a single `α i` must repeat `g i` only, and then
  vanishes because `matAd (g i) (g i) = 0`.

## Generators (`LieGens`)

`LieGens wt κ` (for a finite type `κ`) consists of:

- weights `α : κ → X` with unique integral coefficients (`coeff_inj`);
- matrices `e i` of weight `α i` and `f i` of weight `−α i`;
- additive characters `χ i : X →+ ℚ`;
- `e_f`: `[e i, f j] = 0` for `i ≠ j`, and `[e i, f i] = charDiag wt (χ i)`.

For `G : LieGens wt κ`:

- `pos` and `neg` are the sets of iterated commutators of the `e i` and of the `f i`.
  `lieSpan` is the `ℚ`-span of `pos`, `neg` and the matrices `charDiag wt (χ i)`.
  `e_mem`, `f_mem` and `charDiag_mem` say that the generators lie in `lieSpan`.
- `coeff_inj_neg`, `α_ne_zero`, `iterComm_e_isWtHom`, `iterComm_f_isWtHom`: auxiliary facts.
- `matAd_mem_span_iterComm`: suppose the commutators of `x` with each generator `g j` lie in
  the span of the diagonal matrices. Then `x` maps each iterated commutator of the `g j` into
  the span of these iterated commutators and the diagonal matrices. The proof is an induction
  on `IterComm` using the Jacobi identity.
- `matAd_e_mem`, `matAd_f_mem`, `matAd_charDiag_mem`: commutators with `e i`, `f i` and the
  diagonal matrices preserve `lieSpan`. For `e i` acting on `pos`, the result is again an
  iterated commutator. For `e i` acting on `neg`, apply `matAd_mem_span_iterComm` with `e_f`.
  The diagonal matrices act by scalars on homogeneous elements.
- `matAd_mem`: `lieSpan` is closed under the commutator. The predicate "`matAd a` preserves
  `lieSpan`" holds for the generators and is closed under commutators by the Jacobi identity,
  so it holds for all iterated commutators. Bilinearity then extends it to the span.

## Weight components

These results assume `DecidableEq X`.

- `mem_span_wtProj`, `wtProj_mem_of_isWtHom`, `lieSpan_le_of_wt`: an element of `lieSpan` of
  weight `μ` lies in every subspace `T` that contains the generators of weight `μ`. That is,
  `T` must contain every iterated commutator of weight `μ` and, when `μ = 0`, the diagonal
  matrices. The proof applies the weight projection `wtProj μ` to a representation of the
  element in the span.
- `exists_eq_smul_e_of_isWtHom`: the weight-`α i` component of `lieSpan` is contained in the
  line `ℚ • e i`.
- `eq_one_or_eq_neg_one_of_isWtHom`: if `lieSpan` has a nonzero element of weight `k • α i`
  with `k ≠ 0`, then `k = ±1`.
- `exists_coeff_of_isWtHom`: the weight of a nonzero homogeneous element of `lieSpan` of
  nonzero weight is a nonnegative or nonpositive integral combination of the `α i`.

The last three results follow from `lieSpan_le_of_wt` and `IterComm.eq_of_eq_smul`.

## Provenance

This is the triangular decomposition `𝔤 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔥 ⊕ 𝔫⁺` of a Lie algebra generated by
Chevalley–Serre-type generators, and the fact that the root spaces of the simple roots are
one-dimensional (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §18.2;
Kac, *Infinite dimensional Lie algebras*, Theorem 1.2). Here it is proved only for the span of
iterated commutators inside a matrix algebra, in the weak form above.
